chunks: From him, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Thabit ibn Sharih, from Dawud al-Abzari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him say: 'It is not permissible to sell dates (tamar) with fresh dates (rutab); the dates are dry and the fresh dates are moist.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling dry dates and fresh dates together in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the prohibition of mixing dry and fresh dates in a single sale to avoid *gharar* (uncertainty) arising from differing states of preservation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise commodity classification to ensure fairness in trade, reflecting the broader principle that items with distinct physical properties and shelf-lives must be transacted separately to prevent dispute.
